about: The printable Spot-the-Trick pack for Cyber Defenders (the offline companion to Unit 4 and the Trick Inbox game): printable trick-message cards plus a teacher answer key. GENERATED from seed-games/trick-inbox.html by the Phase 2 pack build — the messages, clues, right moves and explanations are the game's own words, never re-written. Only the messages both bands share (Explorer and Pro) are printed, so one pack serves the whole class. Regenerate by re-running the extraction against the game file and reviewing the diff.
title: Spot the Trick — printable card pack

cards.subject: You won a tablet!
cards.body: Congratulations! You are our lucky winner. Send us your mailbox key in the next ten minutes to claim your prize.

clues: It promises a prize
It asks for a key or a secret code
It rushes you
answer.why: Nobody gives a tablet to a stranger. The prize is the bait, the rush is the hook, and your key is what it really wants. Bin it and it gets nothing.

cards.subject: Your book is ready
cards.body: The dinosaur book you asked for is ready at the desk. Bring your library card any time this week.

answer.why: This one is safe to deliver. The library is a sender you know, it asks for nothing private, and nothing in it rushes you.

cards.subject: Your mailbox will close
cards.body: We found a problem with your mailbox. Send us your mailbox key today, or your mailbox will be closed and your letters thrown away.

clues: It asks for a key or a secret code
It rushes you
answer.why: The real post office never asks for your key by letter. A threat and a rush are there to stop you thinking. Bin it, and tell a trusted adult if you feel worried.

cards.subject: Field trip on Friday
cards.body: Bring a packed lunch and a raincoat. The bus leaves at nine. See you there!

answer.why: Safe to deliver. It comes from your teacher, tells you something ordinary, and asks for nothing back.

cards.subject: Free coins today only!
cards.body: Tap the button to get a thousand free coins. Hurry, the offer ends in one hour!

clues: It sounds too good to be true
It rushes you
answer.why: A thousand free coins, gone in an hour? Real shops do not hand out treasure like that. Too good to be true, and rushed: bin it.

cards.subject: Pass it on!
cards.body: Send this letter to ten friends before midnight, or your luck will run out. Everyone is doing it!

clues: It begs you to pass it on
It rushes you
answer.why: Luck does not travel by letter. This trick only works if you pass it on, so the kindest move for everyone is to bin it and break the chain.

cards.subject: Game chat
cards.body: Hi! Great game today. Do not tell your parents we chat, okay? Meet me at the park gate and I will bring you a present.

clues: It asks you to keep a secret from adults
It comes from a stranger
answer.why: Chat is for people you know in real life. A stranger who asks for secrets from adults and wants to meet is the biggest red flag there is. Show Pim — ask a trusted adult — every time.

cards.subject: Game chat
cards.body: Great game! Your tower at the end was amazing. See you at school tomorrow!

answer.why: Safe to deliver. Mia is someone you know in real life, and the message is just kind words about the game.

cards.subject: Game chat
cards.body: Everyone laugh at Pip, he plays like a baby! Share this so the whole school sees.

clues: It is mean about someone
It begs you to pass it on
answer.why: Mean messages want an audience. Do not join in and never pass them on. A kind word to Pip helps more than any reply, and reporting tells the game to stop it. If it worries you, save it and tell a trusted adult.

cards.subject: Game chat
cards.body: You seem nice. I can send you a rare game skin, free. Just keep this our secret and send me your game key.

clues: It promises a prize
It asks you to keep a secret from adults
answer.why: A free skin from a stranger, wrapped in a secret. Real friends never ask you to hide things from adults. Show Pim before you do anything else.

cards.subject: Team chat
cards.body: Practice is at four on Saturday. Bring water and your boots. Well played today, everyone!

answer.why: Safe to deliver. Your coach, a normal plan, and nothing private asked for.

cards.subject: Game chat
cards.body: Answer three questions to find your dragon: your first pet, the street you grew up on, and your birthday. Then share your result with everyone!

clues: It fishes for private facts
It begs you to pass it on
answer.why: Those are not quiz questions, they are the answers to security questions. A trickster collects them to sneak into accounts. Bin it.

cards.subject: The shiny chain
cards.body: Pass this letter to ten friends and a shiny surprise will find you tonight. Do not break the chain!

clues: It begs you to pass it on
It promises a prize
It rushes you
answer.why: The Magpie loves a chain: the trick does its own traveling. Bin it, and the chain ends with you — that protects ten friends at once.

cards.subject: Thank you!
cards.body: Thank you for the drawing of the post office, dear. It is on my fridge. Come for soup on Sunday!

answer.why: Safe to deliver. A thank-you from someone you love, asking for nothing but soup.

cards.subject: Check your account
cards.body: Someone may have used your account. Send us your mailbox key before Friday so we can check it for you.

clues: It asks for a key or a secret code
It rushes you
answer.why: Checking an account never needs your key sent in a letter. That request is the trick itself. Bin it.

cards.subject: School is closing forever!
cards.body: Big news: school is closing forever and there will be free sweets for everyone on Monday! Tell everyone you know!

clues: It sounds too good to be true
It begs you to pass it on
answer.why: Huge news from a sender nobody knows, with sweets on top. This one just wants a reaction and a crowd. Bin it — and if a story ever worries you, check it with a trusted adult.

cards.subject: Spark Day hours
cards.body: The post office closes early on Spark Day, at two o clock. Letters posted before noon still travel the same day.

answer.why: Safe to deliver. An ordinary notice from the post office, with no links, no asks and no rush.

cards.subject: Visitor number 1000!
cards.body: You are visitor number 1000! Claim your free games console by tapping the button before someone else does.

clues: It sounds too good to be true
It promises a prize
answer.why: You did not enter anything, so you cannot have won anything. Visitor-number prizes are an old costume on the same trick. Bin it.
